body.text:
(#Vaidya 254#)
#Sukhāvatīvyūhaḥ |# (saṃkṣiptamātṛkā |)
body.translated_text: <s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s> (Array of the Land of Bliss) (Shorter Version)

body.text: || namaḥ sarvajñāya ||
body.translated_text: Homage to the Omniscient One.

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam | ekasmin samaye bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhamardhatrayodaśabhirbhikṣuśatairabhijñātābhijñātaiḥ sthavirairmahāśrāvakaiḥ sarvairarhadbhiḥ | tadyathā - sthavireṇa ca śāriputreṇa, mahāmaudgalyāyanena ca mahākāśyapena ca mahākapphiṇena ca mahākātyāyanena ca mahākauṣṭhilena ca revatena ca śuddhipanthakena ca nandena ca ānandena ca rāhulena ca gavāṃpatinā ca bharadvājena ca kālodayinā ca vakkulena ca aniruddhena ca | etaiścānyaiśca saṃbahulairmahāśrāvakaiḥ | saṃbahulaiśca bodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ | tadyathā mañjuśriyā ca kumārabhūtena, ajitena ca bodhisattvena, gandhahastinā ca bodhisattvena, nityodyuktena ca bodhisattvena, anikṣiptadhureṇa ca bodhisattvena | etaiścānyaiśca saṃbahulairbodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ | śakreṇa ca devānāmindreṇa, brahmaṇā ca sahāṃpatinā | etaiśvānyaiśca saṃbahulairdevaputranayutaśatasahasraiḥ || Sukhs_1 ||
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One) was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great assembly of monks—twelve hundred and fifty <s>bhikṣus</s>, all well-known and recognized, elders, great <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), all <s>Arhats</s>. That is to say: the elder <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, <s>Mahākapphiṇa</s>, <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, <s>Mahākauṣṭhila</s>, <s>Revata</s>, <s>Śuddhipanthaka</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Rāhula</s>, <s>Gavāṃpati</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Kālodayin</s>, <s>Vakkula</s>, and <s>Aniruddha</s>—together with these and many other great <s>śrāvakas</s>, and with many <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>. That is to say: the youth <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Ajita</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Gandhahastī</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Nityodyukta</s>, and the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Anikṣiptadhura</s>—together with these and many other <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>mahāsattvas</s>, and with <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, and <s>Brahma Sahāṃpati</s>—together with these and many other hundreds of thousands of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>devaputras</s>. || Sukhs_1 ||

body.text: tatra khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputramāmantrayati sma - asti śāriputra paścime digbhāge ito buddhakṣetraṃ koṭiśatasahasraṃ buddhākṣetrāṇāmatikramya sukhāvatī nāma lokadhātuḥ | tatra amitāyurnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha etarhi tiṣṭhati dhriyate yāpayati, dharmaṃ ca deśayati tatkiṃ manyase śāriputra kena kāraṇena sā lokadhātuḥ sukhāvatītyucyate? tatra khalu punaḥ śāriputra sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau nāsti sattvānāṃ kāyaduḥkhaṃ na cittaduḥkham | apramāṇānyeva sukhakāraṇāni | tena kāraṇena sā lokadhātuḥ sukhāvatītyucyate || Sukhs_2 ||
body.translated_text: There the <s>Bhagavat</s> addressed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'O <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the western direction, beyond a hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddha</s>-fields from here, there is a world-system called <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss). There, a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Amitāyus</s> (Infinite Life), an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One, now dwells, abides, and lives, and teaches the <s>Dharma</s>. What do you think, <s>Śāriputra</s>, for what reason is that world-system called <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss)? Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, in that world-system of <s>Sukhāvatī</s>, there is no bodily suffering for beings, nor mental suffering. The causes of happiness are immeasurable. For that reason, that world-system is called <s>Sukhāvatī</s>.' || Sukhs_2 ||

body.text: punaraparaṃ śāriputra sukhāvatī lokadhātuḥ saptabhirvedikābhiḥ saptabhistālapaṅktibhiḥ kiṅkiṇījālaiśca samalaṃkṛtā samantato 'nupatikṣiptā citrā darśanīyā caturṇāṃ ratnānām | tadyathā suvarṇasya rūpyasya vaiḍūryasya sphaṭikasya | evaṃrūpaiḥ śāriputra buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaṃ tadbuddhakṣetram || Sukhs_3 ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the world-system <s>Sukhāvatī</s> is adorned with seven railings, seven rows of palm trees, and nets of tinkling bells, arranged all around, variegated, beautiful to behold, of four precious materials—that is to say: gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), and crystal. With such arrays of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is that <s>Buddha</s>-field adorned. || Sukhs_3 ||

body.text: punaraparaṃ śāriputra sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātau saptaratnamayyaḥ puṣkariṇyaḥ - tadyathā suvarṇasya rūpyasya vaiḍūryasya sphaṭikasya lohitamuktasya aśmagarbhasya musāragalvasya saptamasya ratnasya | aṣṭāṅgopetavāriparipūrṇāḥ samatīrthakāḥ kākapeyā suvarṇavālukāsaṃstṛtāḥ | tāsu ca puṣkariṇīṣu samantāccaturdiśaṃ catvāri sopānāni citrāṇi darśanīyāni caturṇāṃ ratnānām - tadyathā suvarṇasya rūpyasya vaiḍūryasya sphaṭikasya | tāsāṃ ca puṣkariṇīnāṃ samantādratnavṛkṣā jātāścitrā darśanīyāḥ saptānāṃ ratnānām - tadyathā suvarṇasya rūpyasya vaiḍūryasya sphaṭikasya lohitamuktasyāśmagarbhasya musāragalvasya saptamasya ratnasya | tāsu ca puṣkariṇīṣu santi padmāni jātāni nīlāni nīlavarṇāni nīlanirbhāsāni nīlanidarśanāni | pītāni pītavarṇāni pītanirbhāsāni pītanidarśanāni | lohitāni lohitavarṇāni lohitanirbhāsāni lohitanidarśanāni | (#Sukhs, Vaidya 255#) avadātāni avadātavarṇāni avadātanirbhāsāni avadātanidarśanāni | citrāṇi citravarṇāni citranirbhāsāni citranidarśanāni śakaṭacakrapramāṇapariṇāhāni | evaṃrūpaiḥ śāriputra buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaṃ tadbuddhakṣetram || Sukhs_4 ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the world-system of <s>Sukhāvatī</s> there are lotus pools made of seven precious substances — that is to say: gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), crystal, red pearl, <s>aśmagarbha</s> (diamond), and <s>musāragalva</s> (coral), the seventh precious substance — filled with water possessing the eight qualities, with banks level to the brim, shallow enough for a crow to drink from, and paved with golden sand. And in those lotus pools, on all four sides, there are four stairways, variegated and beautiful to behold, made of four precious substances — that is to say: gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, and crystal. And around those lotus pools, jewel-trees have grown, variegated and beautiful to behold, made of seven precious substances — that is to say: gold, silver, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, crystal, red pearl, <s>aśmagarbha</s>, and <s>musāragalva</s>, the seventh precious substance. And in those lotus pools, lotuses have grown — blue ones of blue color, blue radiance, and blue appearance; yellow ones of yellow color, yellow radiance, and yellow appearance; red ones of red color, red radiance, and red appearance; white ones of white color, white radiance, and white appearance; variegated ones of variegated color, variegated radiance, and variegated appearance — as large in circumference as a chariot-wheel. With such arrays of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is that <s>Buddha</s>-field adorned.

body.text: punaraparaṃ śāriputra tatra buddhakṣetre nityapravāditāni divyāni tūryāṇi | suvarṇavarṇā ca mahāpṛthivī ramaṇīyā | tatra ca buddhakṣetre triṣkṛtvo rātrau triṣkṛtvo divasasya puṣpavarṣaṃ pravarṣati divyānāṃ māndāravapuṣpāṇām | tatra ye sattvā upapannāste ekena purobhaktena koṭiśatasahasraṃ buddhānāṃ vandanti anyāṃllokadhātūn gatvā | ekaikaṃ ca tathāgataṃ koṭiśatasahasrābhiḥ puṣpavṛṣṭibhirabhyavakīrya punarapi tāmeva lokadhātumāgacchanti divāvihārāya | evaṃrūpaiḥ śāriputra buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaṃ tadbuddhakṣetram || Sukhs_5 ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, in that <s>Buddha</s>-field, divine musical instruments are constantly played. The great earth is golden in color and delightful. And in that <s>Buddha</s>-field, three times during the night and three times during the day, a shower of divine <s>māndārava</s> flowers rains down. Those beings who have been reborn there, in a single morning meal-time, go to other world-systems and worship a hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, showering each <s>Tathāgata</s> with a hundred thousand <s>koṭīs</s> of flower-showers; and they return again to that very world-system for the day's rest. With such arrays of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is that <s>Buddha</s>-field adorned.

body.text: punaraparaṃ śāriputra tatra buddhakṣetre santi haṃsāḥ krauñcā mayūrāśca | te triṣkṛtvo rātro triṣkṛtvo divasasya saṃnipatya saṃgītiṃ kurvanti sma, svakasvakāni ca rutāni pravyāharanti | teṣāṃ pravyāharatāmindriyabalabodhyaṅgaśabdo niścarati | tatra teṣāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ taṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā buddhamanasikāra utpadyate, dharmamanasikāra utpadyate, saṃghamanasikāra utpadyate | tatkiṃ manyase śāriputra tiryagyonigatāste sattvāḥ? na punarevaṃ draṣṭvyam | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? nāmāpi śāriputra tatra buddhakṣetre nirayāṇāṃ nāsti, tiryagyonīnāṃ yamalokasya nāsti | te punaḥ pakṣisaṃghāstenāmitāyuṣā tathāgatena nirmitā dharmaśabdaṃ niścārayanti | evaṃrūpaiḥ śāriputra buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaṃ tadbuddhakṣetram || Sukhs_6 ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, in that <s>Buddha</s>-field there are geese, herons, and peacocks. Three times during the night and three times during the day, they gather together and perform a chorus, each uttering its own song. As they sing, the sound of the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), and <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening) issues forth. When those people hear that sound, mindfulness of the <s>Buddha</s> arises in them, mindfulness of the <s>Dharma</s> arises, and mindfulness of the <s>Saṃgha</s> arises. What do you think, <s>Śāriputra</s> — are those beings reborn in the animal realm? This should not be so regarded. For what reason? In that <s>Buddha</s>-field, <s>Śāriputra</s>, not even the name of the hells exists, nor of the animal realm, nor of the realm of <s>Yama</s>. Rather, those flocks of birds have been created by the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, and they send forth the sound of the <s>Dharma</s>. With such arrays of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is that <s>Buddha</s>-field adorned.

body.text: punaraparaṃ śāriputra tatra buddhakṣetre tāsāṃ ca tālapaṅktīnāṃ teṣāṃ ca kiṅkiṇījālānāṃ vāteritānāṃ valgurmanojñaḥ śabdo niścarati - tadyathāpi nāma śāriputra koṭiśatasahasrāṅgikasya divyasya tūryasya cāryaiḥ saṃpravāditasya valgurmanojñaḥ śabdo niścarati, evameva śāriputra tāsāṃ ca tālapaṅktīnāṃ teṣāṃ ca kiṅkiṇījālānāṃ vāteritānāṃ valgurmanojñaḥ śabdo niścarati | tatra teṣāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ taṃ śabdaṃ śrutvā buddhānusmṛtiḥ kāye saṃtiṣṭhati, dharmānusmṛtiḥ kāye saṃtiṣṭhati, saṃghānusmṛtiḥ kāye saṃtiṣṭhati | evarūpaiḥ śāriputra buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaiḥ samalaṃkṛtaṃ tadbuddhakṣetram || Sukhs_7 ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, in that <s>Buddha</s>-field, from those rows of palm trees and those nets of tinkling bells, when stirred by the wind, a sweet and delightful sound issues forth — just as, <s>Śāriputra</s>, from a divine musical instrument of a hundred thousand <s>koṭī</s> parts, when played by noble ones, a sweet and delightful sound issues forth, even so, <s>Śāriputra</s>, from those rows of palm trees and those nets of tinkling bells, when stirred by the wind, a sweet and delightful sound issues forth. When those people hear that sound, <s>buddhānusmṛti</s> (recollection of the <s>Buddha</s>) becomes established in their bodies, <s>dharmānusmṛti</s> (recollection of the <s>Dharma</s>) becomes established in their bodies, and <s>saṃghānusmṛti</s> (recollection of the <s>Saṃgha</s>) becomes established in their bodies. With such arrays of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is that <s>Buddha</s>-field adorned.

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase śāriputra kena kāraṇena sa tathāgato 'mitāyurnāmocyate? tasya khalu punaḥ śāriputra tathāgatasya teṣāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāmaparimitamāyuḥpramāṇam | tena kāraṇena sa tathāgato 'mitāyurnāmocyate | tasya ca śāriputra tathāgatasya daśa kalpā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhasya || Sukhs_8 ||
body.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Śāriputra</s>, for what reason is that <s>Tathāgata</s> called <s>Amitāyus</s> (Infinite Life)? For those humans, <s>Śāriputra</s>, and for that <s>Tathāgata</s>, the measure of life is unlimited. For that reason, that <s>Tathāgata</s> is called <s>Amitāyus</s>. And <s>Śāriputra</s>, ten <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) have passed since that <s>Tathāgata</s> attained unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase śāriputra kena kāraṇena sa tathāgato 'mitābho nāmocyate? tasya khalu punaḥ śāriputra tathāgatasyābhā apratihatā sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu | tena kāraṇena sa tathāgato 'mitābho nāmocyate | tasya ca śāriputra tathāgatasyāprameyaḥ śrāvakasaṃgho yeṣāṃ na sukaraḥ pramāṇamākhyātuḥ śuddhānāmarhatām | evaḥrūpaiḥ śāriputra buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhaiḥ samalaḥkṛtaḥ tadbuddhakṣetram || Sukhs_9 ||
body.translated_text: What do you think, <s>Śāriputra</s>, for what reason is that <s>Tathāgata</s> called <s>Amitābha</s> (Infinite Light)? The radiance of that <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is unobstructed in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields. For that reason, that <s>Tathāgata</s> is called <s>Amitābha</s>. And <s>Śāriputra</s>, that <s>Tathāgata</s> has an immeasurable assembly of <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), who are pure <s>Arhats</s>, whose number is not easy to declare. With such arrays of <s>Buddha</s>-field qualities, <s>Śāriputra</s>, that <s>Buddha</s>-field is adorned.

body.text: punaraparaṃ śāriputra ye amitāyuṣastathāgatasya buddhakṣetre sattvā upapannāḥ śuddhā bodhisattvā avinivartanīyā ekajātipratibaddhāsteṣāṃ śāriputra bodhisattvānāṃ na sukaraṃ pramāṇa#mā#khyātumanyatrāprameyāsaṃkhyeyā (#Sukhs, Vaidya 256#) iti gacchanti | tatra khalu punaḥ śāriputra buddhakṣetre sattvaiḥ praṇidhānaṃ kartavyam | tatkasmāddhetoḥ? yatra hi nāma tathārūpaiḥ satpuruṣaiḥ saha samavadhānaṃ bhavati | nāvaramātrakeṇa śāriputra kuśalamūlena amitāyuṣastathāgatasya buddhakṣetre sattvā upapadyante | yaḥ kaścicchāriputra kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tasya bhagavato 'mitāyuṣastathāgatasya nāmadheyaṃ śroṣyati, śrutvā ca manasikariṣyati, ekarātraṃ vā dvirātraṃ vā trirātraṃ vā catūrātraṃ vā pañcarātraṃ vā ṣaḍrātraṃ vā saptarātraṃ vāvikṣiptacitto manasikariṣyati, yadā sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā kālaṃ kariṣyati, tasya kālaṃ kurvataḥ so 'mitāyustathāgataḥ śrāvakasaṃghaparivṛto bodhisattvaguṇapuraskṛtaḥ purataḥ sthāsyati | so 'viparyastacittaḥ kālaṃ kariṣyati ca | sa kālaṃ kṛtvā tasyaivāmitāyuṣastathāgatasya buddhakṣetre sukhāvatyāṃ lokadhātāvupapatsyate | tasmāttarhi śāriputra idamarthavaśaṃ saṃpaśyamāna eva vadāmi - satkṛtya kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā tatra buddhakṣetre cittapraṇidhānaṃ kartavyam || Sukhs_10 ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, those beings who have been reborn in the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s> are pure <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, non-retrogressing (<s>avinivartanīya</s>), bound to one more birth (<s>ekajātipratibaddha</s>); the number of those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is not easy to declare — they are reckoned as immeasurable and innumerable (<s>aprameyāsaṃkhyeya</s>). Moreover, <s>Śāriputra</s>, beings should make a vow (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) [to be reborn] in that <s>Buddha</s>-field. Why? Because there one comes to be in the company of such excellent beings. It is not, <s>Śāriputra</s>, by a mere trifle of wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) that beings are reborn in the <s>Buddha</s>-field of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>. If any son or daughter of good family will hear the name of the Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, and having heard it, will bear it in mind — for one night, or two nights, or three nights, or four nights, or five nights, or six nights, or seven nights — with undistracted mind, then when that son or daughter of good family comes to die, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, surrounded by an assembly of <s>śrāvakas</s> and attended by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, will stand before them. That person will die with unconfused mind. And having died, that person will be reborn in the world-system <s>Sukhāvatī</s> (Land of Bliss), the <s>Buddha</s>-field of that very <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>. Therefore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, seeing this advantage, I say: every son or daughter of good family should respectfully make a vow of the mind directed toward that <s>Buddha</s>-field.

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma śāriputra ahametarhi tāṃ parikīrtayāmi, evameva śāriputra pūrvasyāṃ diśi akṣobhyo nāma tathāgato merudhvajo nāma tathāgato mahāmerurnāma tathāgato meruprabhāso nāma tathāgato mañjudhvajo nāma tathāgataḥ | evaṃpramukhāḥ śāriputra pūrvasyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopamā buddhā bhagavantaḥ svakasvakāni buddhakṣetrāṇi jihvendriyeṇa saṃchādayitvā nirveṭhanaṃ kurvanti | pratīyatha yūyamidamacintyaguṇaparikīrtanaṃ sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyam || Sukhs_11 ||
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Śāriputra</s>, I now proclaim that [land], so too, <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the eastern direction, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Akṣobhya</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Merudhvaja</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Mahāmeru</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Meruprabhāsa</s>, and the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Mañjudhvaja</s> — these and other <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones in the eastern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, each covering their own <s>Buddha</s>-fields with their tongue and making a proclamation, [declare:] 'Believe in this <s>Dharma</s> discourse called the Proclamation of Inconceivable Qualities, Embraced by All <s>Buddhas</s>!'

body.text: evaṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi candrasūryapradīpo nāma tathāgato yaśaḥprabho nāma tathāgato mahārciḥskandho nāma tathāgato merupradīpo nāma tathāgato 'nantavīryo nāma tathāgataḥ | evaṃpramukhāḥ śāriputra dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopamā buddhā bhagavantaḥ svakasvakāni buddhakṣetrāṇi jihvendriyeṇa saṃchādayitvā nirveṭhanaṃ kurvanti | pratīyatha yūyamidamacintyaguṇaparikīrtanaṃ sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyam || Sukhs_12 ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, in the southern direction, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Candrasūryapradīpa</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Yaśaḥprabha</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Mahārciskandha</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Merupradīpa</s>, and the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Anantavīrya</s> — these and other <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones in the southern direction, as numerous as the sands of the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, each covering their own <s>Buddha</s>-fields with their tongue and making a proclamation, [declare:] 'Believe in this <s>Dharma</s> discourse called the Proclamation of Inconceivable Qualities, Embraced by All <s>Buddhas</s>!'

body.text: evaṃ paścimāyāṃ diśi amitāyurnāma tathāgato 'mitaskandho nāma tathāgato 'mitadhvajo nāma tathāgato mahāprabho nāma tathāgato mahāratnaketurnāma tathāgataḥ śuddharaśmiprabho nāma tathāgataḥ | evaṃpramukhāḥ śāriputra paścimāyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopamā buddhā bhagavantaḥ svakasvakāni buddhakṣetrāṇi jihvendriyeṇa saṃchādayitvā nirveṭhanaṃ kurvanti | pratīyatha yūyamidamacintyaguṇaparikīrtanaṃ sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyam || Sukhs_13 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, in the western direction: the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Amitāyus</s> (Infinite Life), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Amitaskandha</s> (Infinite Aggregate), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Amitadhvaja</s> (Infinite Banner), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Mahāprabha</s> (Great Radiance), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Mahāratnaketu</s> (Great Jewel Standard), and the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śuddharaśmiprabha</s> (Pure-Rayed Radiance). Led by these and others, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the western direction, <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River, covering their own respective <s>Buddha</s>-fields with the organ of their tongues, make a proclamation: 'Trust in this <s>Dharma</s> discourse called the Praise of Inconceivable Qualities, Embraced by All <s>Buddhas</s>.' || Sukhs_13 ||

body.text: evamuttarāyāṃ diśi mahārciḥskandho nāma tathāgato vaiśvānaranirghoṣo nāma tathāgato dundubhisvaranirghoṣo nāma tathāgato duṣpradharṣo nāma tathāgataḥ ādityasaṃbhavo nāma tathāgato jaleniprabho nāma tathāgataḥ prabhākaro nāma tathāgataḥ | evaṃpramukhāḥ śāriputra uttarāyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopamā buddhā bhagavantaḥ svakasvakāni buddhakṣetrāṇi jihvendriyeṇa saṃchādayitvā nirveṭhanaṃ kurvanti | pratīyatha yūyamidamacintyaguṇaparikīrtanaṃ sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyam || Sukhs_14 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, in the northern direction: the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Mahārciskandha</s> (Great Flame Aggregate), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Vaiśvānaranirghoṣa</s> (Sound of Universal Fire), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dundubhisvaranirghoṣa</s> (Sound of the Drum), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Duṣpradharṣa</s> (Invincible), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ādityasaṃbhava</s> (Sun-Born), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Jaleniprabha</s> (Net-of-Water Radiance), and the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Prabhākara</s> (Light-Maker). Led by these and others, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the northern direction, <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River, covering their own respective <s>Buddha</s>-fields with the organ of their tongues, make a proclamation: 'Trust in this <s>Dharma</s> discourse called the Praise of Inconceivable Qualities, Embraced by All <s>Buddhas</s>.' || Sukhs_14 ||

body.text: (#Sukhs, Vaidya 257#) evamadhastāyāṃ diśi siṃho nāma tathāgato yaśo nāma tathāgato yaśaḥprabhāso nāma tathāgato dharmo nāma tathāgato dharmadharo nāma tathāgato dharmadhvajo nāma tathāgataḥ | evaṃpramukhāḥ śāriputra adhastāyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopamā buddhā bhagavantaḥ svakasvakāni buddhakṣetrāṇi jihvendriyeṇa saṃchādayitvā nirveṭhanaṃ kurvanti | pratīyatha yūiyamidamacintyaguṇaparikīrtanaṃ sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyam || Sukhs_15 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, in the downward direction: the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Siṃha</s> (Lion), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Yaśas</s> (Fame), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Yaśaḥprabhāsa</s> (Radiance of Fame), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmadhara</s> (Dharma-Bearer), and the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Dharmadhvaja</s> (Dharma-Banner). Led by these and others, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the downward direction, <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River, covering their own respective <s>Buddha</s>-fields with the organ of their tongues, make a proclamation: 'Trust in this <s>Dharma</s> discourse called the Praise of Inconceivable Qualities, Embraced by All <s>Buddhas</s>.' || Sukhs_15 ||

body.text: evamupariṣṭhāyāṃ diśi brahmaghoṣo nāma tathāgato nakṣatrarājo nāma tathāgata indraketudhvajarājo nāma tathāgato gandhottamo nāma tathāgato gandhaprabhāso nāma tathāgato mahārciskandho nāma tathāgato ratnakusumasaṃpuṣpitagātro nāma tathāgataḥ sālendrarājo nāma tathāgato ratnotpalaśrīrnāma tathāgataḥ sarvārthadarśī nāma tathāgataḥ sumerukalpo nāma tathāgataḥ | evaṃpramukhāḥ śāriputra upariṣṭhāyāṃ diśi gaṅgānadīvālukopamā buddhā bhagavantaḥ svakasvakāni buddhakṣetrāṇi jihvendriyeṇa saṃchādayitvā nirveṭhanaṃ kurvanti | pratīyatha yūyamidamacintyaguṇaparikīrtanaṃ sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyam || Sukhs_16 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, in the upward direction: the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Brahmaghoṣa</s> (Voice of Brahmā), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Nakṣatrarāja</s> (King of Stars), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Indraketudhvajarāja</s> (King of Indra's Banner Standard), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Gandhottama</s> (Supreme Fragrance), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Gandhaprabhāsa</s> (Fragrance Radiance), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Mahārciskandha</s> (Great Flame Aggregate), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnakusumasaṃpuṣpitagātra</s> (Jewel-Flower-Adorned Body), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sālendrarāja</s> (King of <s>Śāla</s>-tree Lords), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Ratnotpalaśrī</s> (Jewel-Lotus Splendor), the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sarvārthadarśin</s> (All-Purpose Seer), and the <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Sumerukalpa</s> (Like Mount Sumeru). Led by these and others, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the upward direction, <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River, covering their own respective <s>Buddha</s>-fields with the organ of their tongues, make a proclamation: 'Trust in this <s>Dharma</s> discourse called the Praise of Inconceivable Qualities, Embraced by All <s>Buddhas</s>.' || Sukhs_16 ||

body.text: tatkiṃ manyase śāriputra kena kāraṇenāyaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ sarvabuddhaparigraho nāmocyate? ye kecicchāriputra kulaputra vā kuladuhitaro vā asya dharmaparyāyasya nāmadheyaṃ śroṣyanti, teṣāṃ va buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ nāmadheyaṃ dhārayiṣyanti, sarve te buddhaparigṛhītā bhaviṣyanti, avinivartanīyāśca bhaviṣyanti anuttarāyāṃ samyaksambodhau | tasmāttarhi śāriputra śraddadhādhvaṃ pratīyatha mā kāṅkṣayatha mama ca teṣāṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatām | ye kecicchāriputra kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā tasya bhagavato 'mitāyuṣastathāgatasya buddhakṣetre cittapraṇidhānaṃ kariṣyanti, kṛtaṃ vā kurvanti vā, sarve te 'vinivartanīyā bhaviṣyantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | tatra ca buddhakṣetra upapatsyanti, upapannā vā upapadyanti vā | tasmāttarhi śāriputra śrāddhaiḥ kulaputraiḥ kuladuhitṛbhiśca tatra buddhakṣetre cittapraṇidhirutpādayitavyaḥ || Sukhs_17 ||
body.translated_text: What do you think, O <s>Śāriputra</s>? For what reason is this <s>Dharma</s> discourse called 'Embraced by All <s>Buddhas</s>'? O <s>Śāriputra</s>, whatever sons of good family or daughters of good family shall hear the name of this <s>Dharma</s> discourse, and shall retain the names of those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones — all of them shall become embraced by the <s>Buddhas</s>, and they shall become non-regressing (<s>avinivartanīya</s>) from unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Therefore, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, believe, trust, and do not doubt — neither in me nor in those <s>Buddhas</s> and Blessed Ones. O <s>Śāriputra</s>, whatever sons of good family or daughters of good family shall make an aspiration (<s>cittapraṇidhāna</s>) toward the <s>Buddha</s>-field of that Blessed <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Amitāyus</s>, have made it, or are making it — all of them shall become non-regressing from unsurpassed perfect awakening. They shall be reborn in that <s>Buddha</s>-field, have been reborn, or are being reborn. Therefore, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, by faithful sons of good family and daughters of good family, the aspiration toward that <s>Buddha</s>-field should be generated. || Sukhs_17 ||

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma śāriputra ahametarhi teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmevamacintyaguṇān parikīrtayāmi, evameva śāriputra mamāpi te buddhā bhagavanta evamacintyaguṇān parikīrtayanti | suduṣkaraṃ bhagavatāṃ śākyamuninā śākyādhirājena kṛtam | sahāyāṃ lokadhātāvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya sarvalokavipratyayanīyo dharmo deśitaḥ kalpakaṣāye sattvakaṣāye dṛṣṭikaṣāya āyuṣkaṣāye kleśakaṣāye || Sukhs_18 ||
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Śāriputra</s>, I now proclaim the inconceivable virtues of those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavats</s>, even so, <s>Śāriputra</s>, those <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavats</s> proclaim my inconceivable virtues [saying]: 'A most difficult thing has been accomplished by the <s>Bhagavat</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the sovereign of the <s>Śākyas</s>. Having attained unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) in the <s>Sahā</s> world-system, he has taught the <s>Dharma</s> that is incredible to the whole world, during the defilement of the age (<s>kalpakaṣāya</s>), the defilement of beings (<s>sattvakaṣāya</s>), the defilement of views (<s>dṛṣṭikaṣāya</s>), the defilement of lifespan (<s>āyuṣkaṣāya</s>), and the defilement of afflictions (<s>kleśakaṣāya</s>).' || Sukhs_18 ||

body.text: tanmamāpi śāriputra paramaduṣkaraṃ yanmayā sahāyāṃ lokadhātāvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya sarvalokavipratyayanīyo dharmo deśitaḥ sattvakaṣāye dṛṣṭikaṣāye kleśakaṣāya āyuṣkaṣāye kalpakaṣāye || Sukhs_19 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, it is extremely difficult for me too that, having attained unsurpassed perfect awakening in the <s>Sahā</s> world-system, I have taught the <s>Dharma</s> that is incredible to the whole world, during the defilement of beings, the defilement of views, the defilement of afflictions, the defilement of lifespan, and the defilement of the age. || Sukhs_19 ||

body.text: idamavocadbhagavānāttamanāḥ | āyuṣmān śāriputraste ca bhikṣavaste ca bodhisattvāḥ sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaśca loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan || Sukhs_20 ||
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavat</s>, with gladdened mind. The venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, those <s>bhikṣus</s>, those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, and the whole world with its gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> rejoiced in the words of the <s>Bhagavat</s>. || Sukhs_20 ||

body.text: sukhāvatīvyūho nāma mahāyānasūtram || (saṃkṣiptamātṛkā |)
body.translated_text: The <s>Mahāyāna sūtra</s> called <s>Sukhāvatīvyūha</s> (Array of the Land of Bliss). (Shorter Version.)
